batch_strategy: Select 32 new condition tuples using interpretable loading contrasts, missing ratio bridges, and targeted extrapolation tests. Give greatest attention to the newly exposed m61 failure, while extending endpoint-specific learning across alcohols, carbonyl compounds, benzoates, and halogenated aromatics. All selected IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions are frozen through this packet hash before any new labels.

choices.reason: m61 at 1/1 and 50 uL establishes the strong-eluent side of its newly problematic low-loading curve. The 5/1 label e75030664990b64e9c05 measured 29.54/47.36 mL, far beyond its acquisition prediction. The current 5.98/11.06 prediction here tests whether that late response is localized near 5/1.

m61 at 2/1 and 50 uL connects the selected 1/1 baseline to e75030664990b64e9c05 at 5/1. Together with the selected 100 uL experiment, it completes a ratio-by-loading comparison against measured 5/1 records e75030664990b64e9c05 and 994a1f65509549a84ede.

m61 at 2/1 and 100 uL completes that controlled comparison. Predictions at 2/1 are almost identical across 50 and 100 uL, whereas measured 5/1 labels differ by 19.28/31.80 mL in onset/completion. This directly tests whether the loading association changes with ratio.

m67 at 5/1 and 150 uL contrasts with low-loading 209cc7cf667dbec940db, measured 11.92/17.20 mL, and extends high-loading 2/1 record 56f8cdbb3999b366d947. It tests whether m61's new loading behavior transfers to the related secondary benzylic alcohol with an ethyl substituent.

m205 at 1/1 and 150 uL completes the loading series after b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8 measured 10.51/25.36 at 50 uL and 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8 measured 18.27/33.28 at 100 uL. The current 14.06/32.05 prediction tests a possible intermediate-loading onset maximum.

m205 at pure EA and 100 uL provides a missing baseline below same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 records 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8/c973d4c257be9ef08216. It separates strong-end extrapolation from the newly observed loading dependence at 1/1; the current prediction is 7.12/15.29 mL.

m203 at 2/1 and 50 uL bridges same-loading 1/1 and 5/1 records d38814bd9947297635d0/5885d427a26f03e522f3. Its predicted 8.91/10.13 mL interval tests a sterically enclosed tertiary alcohol whose endpoint coupling may differ from the open-chain alcohols.

m212 at 2/1 and 50 uL tests the early response of a secondary amine. At 5/1, low-loading d5234e966aa231be05e5 and middle-loading 252c027cf5a42b92c953 measured 7.24/13.67 and 22.07/37.18 mL. This new ratio helps localize that strong loading association instead of transferring an alcohol correction.

m211 at pure EA and 100 uL establishes an unmeasured baseline for phenylpyridine below same-loading 1/1 record a7990e0922fe119d57a6. Comparison with the longer pure-EA quinoline response in ae187d6f3746213b630c tests how strong-end completion transfers across aromatic nitrogen environments.

m78 at 20/1 and 50 uL contrasts with a44a22945d76c02aa6a7 at 100 uL. At 50/1, 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760/61771d230b285babe4b6 showed later low-loading onset but nearly unchanged completion. This determines whether that endpoint-specific association already occurs at 20/1.

m128 at 10/1 and 100 uL completes a useful loading series. The current V2 prediction, 52.06 mL, is below both measured loading endpoints: 54.40 in 2f72c334253bbe94a8ab and 57.29 in 596bd04bfe916866f908. The label tests this predicted middle-loading minimum without imposing monotonicity.

m114 at 10/1 and 100 uL fills a missing ratio between same-loading 2/1 record a5583432158c4e0d0cbb and 20/1 record 8232ed63909910ce88f2. Its predicted 6.78/23.68 mL response tests where onset begins rising for a methoxy-substituted diaryl ketone.

m127 at 5/1 and 50 uL starts a matched pair with the selected 10/1 row. Predictions decrease from 9.46/21.60 to 8.28/19.86 mL as eluent weakens. The pair tests this unverified reversal below measured 20/1 record 8143c4fff6f999b7ad0e, away from its irregular 50/1 loading records.

m127 at 10/1 and 50 uL completes that ratio pair and adds a direct loading comparison with aff2ffd59a0610a54995 at 100 uL. It distinguishes a genuine low-loading response reversal from propagation of unusual onset behavior across the ortho-methoxy acetophenone curve.

m172 at 20/1 and 100 uL extends its measured 5/1–10/1 response, including b54f29a73518aa1f30a7/c4b2566e6fe1d00b20ea. The predicted 8.77/28.27 mL response tests transfer to a cyclopropyl ketone with a fluorobenzyl group. Its high CW distance adds coverage value.

m185 at 20/1 and 100 uL extends same-loading 2/1 anchor a134ef1942ffcd81d017 and bridges toward the 50/1 low-loading label 6c28e50241ca84637c9f. It tests response growth for a doubly ortho-fluorinated aldehyde against the flatter onset of related ortho-brominated carbonyl compounds, retaining loading differences.

m196 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends same-loading 20/1 record ffa53b3aa054bc392704, measured 6.13/24.44 mL. The predicted 13.56/34.83 response tests the onset transition of a brominated naphthaldehyde, with m195 record 8bef7f788af60df5e18a providing a structural reference under different recorded loading conditions.

m101 at 20/1 and 68.02721088 uL sample starts a fixed-loading pair with 50/1. Same-loading 10/1 record 65e9c139dc66fe608a89 measured 9.66/23.13 mL. The predicted 15.38/26.77 response tests unequal onset and completion growth for a bromomethyl-substituted benzoate.

m101 at 50/1 and the same sample/loading-solvent volumes completes that ratio pair. Its predicted 22.66/37.43 mL response extends an otherwise unmeasured weak-eluent region. Together, the two labels teach curve shape rather than a single substituent offset; high CW distance supports their coverage value.

m55 at 40/1 and 100 uL extends the measured 20/1 response in 7937e75a777f4bf48438. The recent m56 50/1 label 5c11321c1ad5aec4ddf1 exposed a completion underestimate. This tests whether that correction transfers across benzoate alkyl-chain environments at the same PE loading-solvent volume.

m56 at 20/1 and 100 uL locates completion growth below same-loading 50/1 record 5c11321c1ad5aec4ddf1, measured 7.03/23.27 mL. Measured 10/1 records 19e665b6098744dfb60c/8e175dc1200d398d3489 use lower/higher loading. This bridge separates onset placement from completion expansion.

m174 at 100/1 and 150 uL tests loading transfer of the comparatively short measured interval at 50 uL in 7f4f64cb791c71ba0420. The current 25.05/38.74 prediction implies earlier onset and later completion at higher loading. This tests endpoint coupling after the previous opposite-signed acquisition errors.

m156 at 20/1 and 50 uL bridges matched-loading 10/1 and 50/1 labels ce2b3297b07008700156/8fa8d7ec035c6a829dc4. Those onsets were nearly unchanged while completion increased by 10.42 mL. This identifies where that completion growth occurs in a low-TPSA aromatic.

m188 at 50/1 and 50 uL completes a new weak-eluent pair with the selected 20/1 row. Same-loading 1/1 record 7bfffb44429fc5d49187 is a sparse strong-end anchor. The pair tests an inadequately measured halobenzaldehyde curve rather than relying on neighboring isomers' predictions.

m192 at 50/1 and 150 uL extends same-loading 1/1 anchor 90b9bfcce4f713fc0a63. This supplies a weak-eluent label for the chlorine-position isomer of m188. Their density and DCM loading-volume differences remain part of the comparison, so the label informs joint structure-condition transfer.

m208 at pure EA and 100 uL establishes an unmeasured iodophenol baseline. Its predicted onset, 9.91 mL, exceeds the selected same-loading 2/1 prediction. Recent strong-end overestimates for m191 and shorter m202 completion motivate checking this extrapolation while allowing genuine local tails.

m208 at 2/1 and 100 uL pairs with its selected pure-EA baseline and contrasts with low-loading e71bdbb1d06ba82dc4cc, measured 6.63/11.63 mL. Holding all loading variables fixed across the selected ratios distinguishes a predicted strong-end reversal from a loading association.

m156 at 5/1 and 50 uL tests the remaining predicted dip, 5.46/8.32 mL, below measured 2/1 record cd3c75eca39365e943e4 and 10/1 record ce2b3297b07008700156. The previous predicted 10/1 onset dip was not observed; this checks whether the artifact has merely shifted to another ratio.

m75 at 1/1 and 50 uL adds an independent ratio reference to the irregular low-loading 2/1 onset in f2312f90dd4cf5ef0e23 and ordinary 5/1 response d0c994e30d2f33948394. The new middle-loading 2/1 label f7684c557ad58e3a1b0b did not reproduce interval collapse, so this is a bounded localization test.

m135 at 10/1 and 150 uL completes the loading series after f433bc672465387d951a and 75232f4ee5de52a0499e measured 47.38/68.38 and 39.39/66.36 mL. The current 44.84/71.22 prediction tests a middle-loading onset minimum and whether completion remains comparatively loading-insensitive.

m37 at 20/1 and 150 uL completes a donor-free nitro-ketone loading series. Low- and middle-loading 606886b17304ec494aa0/b6f1b33a5491968c645e measured 53.14/97.19 and 45.32/95.57 mL. It tests whether the onset decrease continues, flattens, or reverses at the largest loading.

m188 at 20/1 and 50 uL provides the intermediate point needed to interpret its selected 50/1 extension against measured 1/1 record 7bfffb44429fc5d49187. The predicted 5.73/16.41 response tests early-onset persistence before weaker-eluent growth, improving transfer across halogenated aldehyde rows.

hypotheses.content: The previous assumption that m61 at 5/1 was a stable region for testing transferable alcohol loading behavior is weakened. Its measured 50 uL response is much later than its 100 uL response. Whether this is localized near 5/1 or reflects a broader recorded loading association remains unresolved; unrecorded variation is also possible.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A large local failure should not become a shared alcohol offset. A matched ratio-by-loading comparison can identify which recorded relationship needs learning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the large 50-versus-100 uL difference recur at 2/1, and does the low-loading 1/1 label remain near its early prediction?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-ratio responses remain motif-specific and endpoint-specific. Recent m128 and m181 bridges were substantially better predicted than their earlier failure points, while m110 and m116 needed smaller, differently directed corrections. Observed onset reversals in m128 also prevent treating monotonic onset as an absolute constraint.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing bridges and restrained extrapolations can teach response placement across carbonyl connectivity, methoxy substitution, halogen environment, and loading conditions without applying a common retention shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the m127 predicted 5/1-to-10/1 reversal and m128 middle-loading completion minimum real, and do the sparsely measured carbonyl extensions follow their predicted response shapes?

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on structure, ratio, and endpoint. m205 completion rises from 50 to 100 uL at 1/1 but is nearly unchanged from 100 to 150 uL at 2/1. m78 at 50/1 changes onset more than completion. The m75 interval collapse did not transfer across loading. These findings support conditional relationships rather than a universal loading direction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current predictor frequently gives nearly flat loading responses. Completing selected loading series and testing transfer across alcohol, amine, ester, and nitro-ketone environments can show where that approximation succeeds or fails.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m205, m135, and m37 loading midpoints or endpoint trends persist at the missing loading, and does m78's onset association extend to 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent benzoate responses can differ substantially between onset and completion. m56 at 50/1 primarily exposed underestimated completion, whereas m174 at 100/1 exposed underestimated onset and overestimated completion. These observations argue against transferring a single weak-eluent correction across ester substituent environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A response bridge, a fixed-loading extension pair, and a loading-transfer test constrain different ways the two endpoints can decouple across a recurring ester family.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m56 completion expand, does m55 share that response, does m101 follow its predicted 20/1–50/1 curve, and does m174's shorter 100/1 interval transfer to higher loading?

hypotheses.content: For m156 at 50 uL, the newly measured 10/1-to-50/1 response has nearly constant onset and appreciable completion growth. The earlier predicted 10/1 onset dip was not observed. A remaining predicted dip at 5/1 and the placement of completion growth at 20/1 are untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This supplies a low-polarity counterexample to response rules learned mainly from polar carbonyls and donors, while separating an onset artifact from a genuine completion response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does 5/1 actually elute earlier than 2/1, and is the measured completion increase gradual through 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Extended strong-eluent completion remains a local structure-condition association. Recent pure-EA m191 and m202 labels were earlier than predicted, while m197 retains a measured tail. The new m194 5/1 high-loading label did not extend completion beyond its 1/1–2/1 high-loading region. Strong-end extrapolation therefore needs local anchors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New baselines for distinct donor and nitrogen environments can limit propagation of valid but local completion tails. The matched m208 ratio pair also tests an unusual predicted strong-end onset response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the pure-EA predictions for m205, m211, and m208 supported, and does m208 still show the predicted onset reversal when loading is held fixed?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest batch substantially reduces the case for repeatedly expanding the previously severe m128 and m181 failures. m128's high-loading 5/1 and 10/1 labels had modest completion underestimates, and m181 at high-loading 10/1 was predicted almost exactly. I retain one informative m128 loading midpoint and move more effort to missing relationships in other structures. The new m116 and m110 labels also support ratio-specific correction rather than a common upward offset.

The largest new failure is m61 at 5/1 and 50 uL: acquisition-time predictions underestimated onset/completion by 21.08/32.37 mL. This contradicts my assumption that this was a stable comparison region. The selected m61 experiments complete a 2/1-versus-5/1, 50-versus-100 uL comparison and add a lower-ratio baseline. I do not assign a mechanism unsupported by the recorded variables.

Loading direction remains conditional. m205 at low-loading 1/1 was much earlier than predicted, while its high-loading 2/1 label was close to the middle-loading anchor. m78 at low-loading 50/1 had later onset with nearly unchanged completion. These outcomes motivate missing loading endpoints and transfer tests across different structural environments.

m125's new 5/1 midpoint, 42.96/73.10 mL, lies near its measured loading-endpoint range. This supports the local interpretation and reduces the urgency of further sample-loading interpolation there. The pure-EA m191 and m202 results further limit broad transfer of strong-end tails.

m156's measured 10/1 onset rejected the predicted dip, while its 50/1 completion exceeded prediction. m56 likewise exposed underestimated completion. In contrast, m174 at 100/1 needed later onset and earlier completion. These opposite endpoint patterns motivate focused response bridges. Finally, m75's middle-loading 2/1 result did not reproduce the low-loading interval collapse; one new strong-side reference is retained to localize that irregularity.
batch_rationale:
The batch combines controlled comparisons with coverage of sparsely measured response regions. The m61 experiments form a particularly discriminating local experiment around the largest recent failure. The m205, m135, and m37 choices complete meaningful loading series, while m67, m203, m212, and m78 test how endpoint-specific loading associations transfer across structure and ratio.

The carbonyl bridges cover methoxy substitution, ketone connectivity, and halogen environments. The m188 pair is valuable because it adds response shape beyond a sparse same-loading strong-end anchor. The benzoate experiments distinguish completion repair from onset repair and extend learning to new weak-eluent conditions. The m156 pair tests a remaining model reversal while locating observed completion growth. Strong-end measurements are limited to structures with missing baselines or a specific predicted reversal.

All 32 choices are distinct supplied candidates with new condition tuples; no pending experiments exist. Duplicate candidate tuples were avoided. Cross-molecule comparisons retain differences in density, sample volume, loading solvent, and loading-solvent volume. High CW distances provide secondary coverage evidence, and single-predictor quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The expected benefit is better joint prediction of V1 and V2 across the Row-distribution after retraining, through localization of failures and learning of transferable structure-condition relationships.
